claim: MLL-rearranged leukemia depends on H3K79 methylation.
source: MLL-rearranged leukemia depends on H3K79 methylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about MLL-rearranged leukemia.

claim: Depletion of H3K79 methylation by DOT1L deletion or high concentrations of pinometostat downregulates HOXA9 and MEIS1.
source: Depletion of this transcriptionally activating mark by DOT1L deletion or high concentrations of the inhibitor pinometostat downregulates HOXA9 and MEIS1, and consequently reduces leukemia survival.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Some MLL-rearranged leukemias are susceptible to low-dose pinometostat, far below concentrations that downregulate the canonical proliferation pathway.
source: Yet, some MLL-rearranged leukemias are inexplicably susceptible to low-dose pinometostat, far below concentrations that downregulate this canonical proliferation pathway.
evidence: This is a key observation from the study presented in the abstract.

claim: H3K79me2 is markedly depleted at pinometostat-downregulated and MLL-fusion targets by ICeChIP-seq.
source: By ICeChIP-seq, H3K79me2 is markedly depleted at pinometostat-downregulated and MLL-fusion targets, with paradoxical increases of H3K4me3 and loss of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from ICeChIP-seq data presented in the study.

claim: Pinometostat treatment causes paradoxical increases of H3K4me3 at MLL-fusion targets.
source: By ICeChIP-seq, H3K79me2 is markedly depleted at pinometostat-downregulated and MLL-fusion targets, with paradoxical increases of H3K4me3 and loss of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: Pinometostat treatment causes loss of H3K27me3.
source: By ICeChIP-seq, H3K79me2 is markedly depleted at pinometostat-downregulated and MLL-fusion targets, with paradoxical increases of H3K4me3 and loss of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: Downregulation of polycomb components accounts for some of the proliferation defect.
source: Although downregulation of polycomb components accounts for some of the proliferation defect, transcriptional downregulation of FLT3 is the major pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study based on experimental data.

claim: Transcriptional downregulation of FLT3 is the major pathway responsible for proliferation defects from low-dose pinometostat.
source: Although downregulation of polycomb components accounts for some of the proliferation defect, transcriptional downregulation of FLT3 is the major pathway.
evidence: This is a major conclusion from the study based on multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Loss-of-FLT3-function recapitulates the cytotoxicity and gene expression consequences of low-dose pinometostat.
source: Loss-of-FLT3-function recapitulates the cytotoxicity and gene expression consequences of low-dose pinometostat, whereas overexpression of constitutively active STAT5A, a target of FLT3-ITD-signaling, largely rescues these defects.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from FLT3 knockdown experiments.

claim: Overexpression of constitutively active STAT5A largely rescues the defects caused by low-dose pinometostat.
source: Loss-of-FLT3-function recapitulates the cytotoxicity and gene expression consequences of low-dose pinometostat, whereas overexpression of constitutively active STAT5A, a target of FLT3-ITD-signaling, largely rescues these defects.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from STAT5A-CA overexpression experiments.

claim: STAT5A is a target of FLT3-ITD-signaling.
source: Loss-of-FLT3-function recapitulates the cytotoxicity and gene expression consequences of low-dose pinometostat, whereas overexpression of constitutively active STAT5A, a target of FLT3-ITD-signaling, largely rescues these defects.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about FLT3-ITD signaling.

claim: The FLT3-STAT5A pathway depends on MLL1.
source: This pathway also depends on MLL1, indicating combinations of DOT1L, MLL1 and FLT3 inhibitors should be explored for treating FLT3-mutant leukemia.
evidence: This is a conclusion from experiments with MLL1 inhibitors.

claim: Combinations of DOT1L, MLL1 and FLT3 inhibitors should be explored for treating FLT3-mutant leukemia.
source: This pathway also depends on MLL1, indicating combinations of DOT1L, MLL1 and FLT3 inhibitors should be explored for treating FLT3-mutant leukemia.
evidence: This is a therapeutic recommendation based on the study findings.

claim: MLL-rearrangements account for ~10% of all leukemia cases.
source: MLL1-rearrangements (MLL-r) account for ~10% of all leukemia cases and are especially prominent in infants (70–80%) and, lacking an effective standard of care, bear a very poor prognosis (Marks et al., 2013; Jabbour et al., 2015; Mann et al., 2010; Pieters et al., 2007; Winters and Bernt, 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-rearrangements are especially prominent in infants (70–80%).
source: MLL1-rearrangements (MLL-r) account for ~10% of all leukemia cases and are especially prominent in infants (70–80%) and, lacking an effective standard of care, bear a very poor prognosis (Marks et al., 2013; Jabbour et al., 2015; Mann et al., 2010; Pieters et al., 2007; Winters and Bernt, 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-rearranged leukemia lacks an effective standard of care and bears a very poor prognosis.
source: MLL1-rearrangements (MLL-r) account for ~10% of all leukemia cases and are especially prominent in infants (70–80%) and, lacking an effective standard of care, bear a very poor prognosis (Marks et al., 2013; Jabbour et al., 2015; Mann et al., 2010; Pieters et al., 2007; Winters and Bernt, 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-rearrangements rely on additional mutations to cause leukemia.
source: A growing body of evidence suggests that MLL-rearrangements rely on additional mutations to cause leukemia.
evidence: This is stated as an emerging understanding from the literature.

claim: Leukemia patients with MLL-fusions often have additional mutations that affect growth signaling pathways.
source: Leukemia patients with MLL-fusions often have additional mutations that affect growth signaling pathways (Grossmann et al., 2013; Liang et al., 2006; Armstrong et al., 2003) and MLL-fusions in mouse models cause leukemias with longer-than-expected latencies, suggesting that additional mutations are required for full progression (Ono et al., 2005; Corral et al., 1996; Forster et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-fusions in mouse models cause leukemias with longer-than-expected latencies.
source: Leukemia patients with MLL-fusions often have additional mutations that affect growth signaling pathways (Grossmann et al., 2013; Liang et al., 2006; Armstrong et al., 2003) and MLL-fusions in mouse models cause leukemias with longer-than-expected latencies, suggesting that additional mutations are required for full progression (Ono et al., 2005; Corral et al., 1996; Forster et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The longer-than-expected latencies of MLL-fusion-induced leukemias in mouse models suggest that additional mutations are required for full progression.
source: Leukemia patients with MLL-fusions often have additional mutations that affect growth signaling pathways (Grossmann et al., 2013; Liang et al., 2006; Armstrong et al., 2003) and MLL-fusions in mouse models cause leukemias with longer-than-expected latencies, suggesting that additional mutations are required for full progression (Ono et al., 2005; Corral et al., 1996; Forster et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference from cited mouse model data.

claim: MLL1 is a histone H3 lysine methyltransferase involved in regulating HOX gene expression during development and normal hematopoiesis.
source: MLL1 (Mixed Lineage Leukemia protein, also known as KMT2A) is a histone H3 lysine methyltransferase involved in regulating HOX gene expression during development and normal hematopoiesis (Hess, 2004).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Translocations of MLL1 fuse its amino terminus to the carboxy-terminus of over 130 different fusion partners.
source: Translocations of MLL1 fuse its amino terminus to the carboxy-terminus of a growing list of over 130 different fusion partners (Meyer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-fusions lack methyltransferase activity.
source: Although these MLL-fusions lack methyltransferase activity, a functional copy of the MLL1 gene is necessary to target and hypermethylate H3K4 at MLL-fusion target genes to induce leukemogenesis (Milne et al., 2005; Cao et al., 2014; Milne et al., 2010).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: A functional copy of the MLL1 gene is necessary to target and hypermethylate H3K4 at MLL-fusion target genes to induce leukemogenesis.
source: Although these MLL-fusions lack methyltransferase activity, a functional copy of the MLL1 gene is necessary to target and hypermethylate H3K4 at MLL-fusion target genes to induce leukemogenesis (Milne et al., 2005; Cao et al., 2014; Milne et al., 2010).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: In more than 75% of AML cases and >90% of ALL cases involving MLL translocations, the MLL-fusion partner is one of seven members of the transcriptional elongation complex.
source: In more than 75% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cases and >90% of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cases involving MLL translocations, the MLL-fusion partner is one of seven members of the transcriptional elongation complex, most commonly, AF9 and AF4, respectively (Marschalek, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: AF9 and AF4 are the most common MLL-fusion partners in AML and ALL, respectively.
source: In more than 75% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cases and >90% of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) cases involving MLL translocations, the MLL-fusion partner is one of seven members of the transcriptional elongation complex, most commonly, AF9 and AF4, respectively (Marschalek, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-fusion partners aberrantly recruit DOT1L to MLL1 target genes including the HOXA gene cluster.
source: These fusion partners aberrantly recruit DOT1L, the sole histone H3 lysine 79 methyltransferase to MLL1 target genes including the HOXA gene cluster (Mohan et al., 2010; Okada et al., 2005; Kerry et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: DOT1L is the sole histone H3 lysine 79 methyltransferase.
source: These fusion partners aberrantly recruit DOT1L, the sole histone H3 lysine 79 methyltransferase to MLL1 target genes including the HOXA gene cluster (Mohan et al., 2010; Okada et al., 2005; Kerry et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: DOT1L-mediated hypermethylation of H3K79 promotes expression of MLL-fusion targets.
source: By mechanisms that remain unclear, DOT1L-mediated hypermethylation of H3K79 promotes expression of MLL-fusion targets (Milne et al., 2005; Bernt et al., 2011; Guenther et al., 2008; Stubbs et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2015a), establishing an expression profile with a surprising degree of target gene overlap across different MLL-fusions (Armstrong et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from published literature, though the mechanism is noted as unclear.

claim: Different MLL-fusions establish an expression profile with a surprising degree of target gene overlap.
source: By mechanisms that remain unclear, DOT1L-mediated hypermethylation of H3K79 promotes expression of MLL-fusion targets (Milne et al., 2005; Bernt et al., 2011; Guenther et al., 2008; Stubbs et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2015a), establishing an expression profile with a surprising degree of target gene overlap across different MLL-fusions (Armstrong et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Ablation of H3K79 methylation through knockout or pharmacological targeting of DOT1L abrogates the MLL-fusion target gene expression profile.
source: Ablation of H3K79 methylation through knockout or pharmacological targeting of DOT1L abrogates the MLL-fusion target gene expression profile, selectively induces apoptosis and differentiation of leukemia cells in culture and dramatically extends the survival of mice in xenograft experiments (Bernt et al., 2011; Daigle et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Ablation of H3K79 methylation selectively induces apoptosis and differentiation of leukemia cells in culture.
source: Ablation of H3K79 methylation through knockout or pharmacological targeting of DOT1L abrogates the MLL-fusion target gene expression profile, selectively induces apoptosis and differentiation of leukemia cells in culture and dramatically extends the survival of mice in xenograft experiments (Bernt et al., 2011; Daigle et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Ablation of H3K79 methylation dramatically extends the survival of mice in xenograft experiments.
source: Ablation of H3K79 methylation through knockout or pharmacological targeting of DOT1L abrogates the MLL-fusion target gene expression profile, selectively induces apoptosis and differentiation of leukemia cells in culture and dramatically extends the survival of mice in xenograft experiments (Bernt et al., 2011; Daigle et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Viral co-transduction of HOXA9 and MEIS1 is sufficient to cause acute leukemia in mouse bone marrow progenitors.
source: Viral co-transduction of the MLL-AF4 targets (Zeisig et al., 2004) HOXA9 and MEIS1 is sufficient to cause acute leukemia in mouse bone marrow progenitors, arguing that these transcription factors represent a major etiologic pathway in MLL-r leukemia (Corral et al., 1996; Chang et al., 2010a; Jo et al., 2011; Kroon et al., 1998; Calvo et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: HOXA9 and MEIS1 are MLL-AF4 targets.
source: Viral co-transduction of the MLL-AF4 targets (Zeisig et al., 2004) HOXA9 and MEIS1 is sufficient to cause acute leukemia in mouse bone marrow progenitors, arguing that these transcription factors represent a major etiologic pathway in MLL-r leukemia (Corral et al., 1996; Chang et al., 2010a; Jo et al., 2011; Kroon et al., 1998; Calvo et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: HOXA9 and MEIS1 represent a major etiologic pathway in MLL-r leukemia.
source: Viral co-transduction of the MLL-AF4 targets (Zeisig et al., 2004) HOXA9 and MEIS1 is sufficient to cause acute leukemia in mouse bone marrow progenitors, arguing that these transcription factors represent a major etiologic pathway in MLL-r leukemia (Corral et al., 1996; Chang et al., 2010a; Jo et al., 2011; Kroon et al., 1998; Calvo et al., 2002).
evidence: This is an inference from cited experimental data.

claim: Exogenous expression of MLL-AF9 in mice requires a long latency period (4–9 months).
source: However, exogenous expression of MLL-AF9 in mice requires a long latency period (4–9 months) and chemotherapy induced MLL-translocations cause disease 3–5 years after treatment, suggesting that additional mutations are required for leukemagenesis (Corral et al., 1996; Dobson et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Chemotherapy induced MLL-translocations cause disease 3–5 years after treatment.
source: However, exogenous expression of MLL-AF9 in mice requires a long latency period (4–9 months) and chemotherapy induced MLL-translocations cause disease 3–5 years after treatment, suggesting that additional mutations are required for leukemagenesis (Corral et al., 1996; Dobson et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The long latency periods suggest that additional mutations are required for leukemagenesis.
source: However, exogenous expression of MLL-AF9 in mice requires a long latency period (4–9 months) and chemotherapy induced MLL-translocations cause disease 3–5 years after treatment, suggesting that additional mutations are required for leukemagenesis (Corral et al., 1996; Dobson et al., 1999).
evidence: This is an inference from cited data.

claim: Pinometostat (EPZ5676) is a highly specific DOT1L inhibitor.
source: Pinometostat (EPZ5676), a highly specific DOT1L inhibitor (Daigle et al., 2013; Daigle et al., 2011; Anglin and Song, 2013; Yu et al., 2012) displays 37,000-fold selectivity over its closest related paralogs and a host of other lysine and arginine methyltransferases.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Pinometostat displays 37,000-fold selectivity over its closest related paralogs and other lysine and arginine methyltransferases.
source: Pinometostat (EPZ5676), a highly specific DOT1L inhibitor (Daigle et al., 2013; Daigle et al., 2011; Anglin and Song, 2013; Yu et al., 2012) displays 37,000-fold selectivity over its closest related paralogs and a host of other lysine and arginine methyltransferases.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Several cell lines with the MLL-AF4 translocation display pinometostat sensitivities that differ by nearly three orders of magnitude.
source: Interestingly, several cell lines that all have the MLL-AF4 translocation display pinometostat sensitivities that differ by nearly three orders of magnitude (Daigle et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MV4;11 displays a pinometostat IC50 for proliferation that is 20 times lower than the IC50 for HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression.
source: One of these lines (MV4;11) displays a pinometostat IC50 for proliferation that is 20 times lower than the IC50 for HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression (Daigle et al., 2013), suggesting that these drivers of leukemogenesis, though downregulated at higher concentrations (1 µM) (Daigle et al., 2013), may not contribute to cell-type-specific effects at lower concentrations.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: HOXA9 and MEIS1 may not contribute to cell-type-specific effects at lower pinometostat concentrations.
source: One of these lines (MV4;11) displays a pinometostat IC50 for proliferation that is 20 times lower than the IC50 for HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression (Daigle et al., 2013), suggesting that these drivers of leukemogenesis, though downregulated at higher concentrations (1 µM) (Daigle et al., 2013), may not contribute to cell-type-specific effects at lower concentrations.
evidence: This is an inference from cited data.

claim: MLL-r cell lines harboring FLT3-ITD mutations are the most susceptible to low-dose pinometostat.
source: We sought to understand low-dose pinometostat effects by treating a variety of MLL-r cell lines with a concentration that reduces proliferation in only a subset, with MLL-r cell lines harboring FLT3-ITD mutations being the most susceptible.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's experiments.

claim: Under low-dose pinometostat conditions, HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression remain unaffected.
source: Under these conditions, HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression remain unaffected, presenting a clear exception to the existing paradigm, but we found thousands of other differentially expressed genes, including the PBX3 and FLT3 oncogenes.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's experiments.

claim: Low-dose pinometostat treatment results in thousands of differentially expressed genes, including PBX3 and FLT3.
source: Under these conditions, HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression remain unaffected, presenting a clear exception to the existing paradigm, but we found thousands of other differentially expressed genes, including the PBX3 and FLT3 oncogenes.
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment observed larger reductions in H3K79me2 density at a subset of MLL-AF4 targets.
source: Capitalizing on the sensitivity of internally calibrated ChIP-seq (ICeChIP-seq) (Grzybowski et al., 2015; Grzybowski et al., 2019), we observed larger reductions in H3K79me2 density at a subset of MLL-AF4 targets, a genome-wide reduction in H3K27me3 and stark H3K4me3 increases at transcription start sites.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment causes a genome-wide reduction in H3K27me3.
source: Capitalizing on the sensitivity of internally calibrated ChIP-seq (ICeChIP-seq) (Grzybowski et al., 2015; Grzybowski et al., 2019), we observed larger reductions in H3K79me2 density at a subset of MLL-AF4 targets, a genome-wide reduction in H3K27me3 and stark H3K4me3 increases at transcription start sites.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment causes stark H3K4me3 increases at transcription start sites.
source: Capitalizing on the sensitivity of internally calibrated ChIP-seq (ICeChIP-seq) (Grzybowski et al., 2015; Grzybowski et al., 2019), we observed larger reductions in H3K79me2 density at a subset of MLL-AF4 targets, a genome-wide reduction in H3K27me3 and stark H3K4me3 increases at transcription start sites.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: DOT1L inhibition downregulated the EZH2 and EED components of the PRC2 complex.
source: In addition, DOT1L inhibition also downregulated the EZH2 and EED components of the PRC2 complex, likely accounting for global reductions in H3K27me3 and imparting modest, but distinct effects on proliferation and a correspondingly moderate proliferation rescue from EZH2 overexpression.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's experiments.

claim: Downregulation of EZH2 and EED likely accounts for global reductions in H3K27me3.
source: In addition, DOT1L inhibition also downregulated the EZH2 and EED components of the PRC2 complex, likely accounting for global reductions in H3K27me3 and imparting modest, but distinct effects on proliferation and a correspondingly moderate proliferation rescue from EZH2 overexpression.
evidence: This is an inference from the study's data.

claim: EZH2 overexpression provides a moderate proliferation rescue from DOT1L inhibition.
source: In addition, DOT1L inhibition also downregulated the EZH2 and EED components of the PRC2 complex, likely accounting for global reductions in H3K27me3 and imparting modest, but distinct effects on proliferation and a correspondingly moderate proliferation rescue from EZH2 overexpression.
evidence: This is a finding from overexpression experiments.

claim: The FLT3-ITD signaling and PRC2 pathways are more sensitive to disruptions of MLL-fusion-mediated gene activation than HOXA9 and MEIS1 in MLL-r, FLT3ITD leukemias.
source: Collectively, our data argue that the FLT3-ITD signaling and PRC2 pathways, are more sensitive to disruptions of MLL-fusion-mediated gene activation than the canonical oncogenic drivers in MLL-r, FLT3ITD leukemias, defining a new molecular understanding of how MLL-fusions cooperate with other oncogenic factors to induce leukemia.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's data.

claim: Pinometostat concentrations as low as 10 nM significantly reduce global levels of H3K79me2.
source: Consonant with previous findings (Daigle et al., 2013), pinometostat concentrations as low as 10 nM significantly reduce global levels of H3K79me2 and cause a 30 ± 10% reduction in MV4;11 proliferation, while 100 nM inhibitor reduced cell proliferation by 80 ± 10% (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 10 nM pinometostat causes a 30 ± 10% reduction in MV4;11 proliferation.
source: Consonant with previous findings (Daigle et al., 2013), pinometostat concentrations as low as 10 nM significantly reduce global levels of H3K79me2 and cause a 30 ± 10% reduction in MV4;11 proliferation, while 100 nM inhibitor reduced cell proliferation by 80 ± 10% (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat reduced MV4;11 cell proliferation by 80 ± 10%.
source: Consonant with previous findings (Daigle et al., 2013), pinometostat concentrations as low as 10 nM significantly reduce global levels of H3K79me2 and cause a 30 ± 10% reduction in MV4;11 proliferation, while 100 nM inhibitor reduced cell proliferation by 80 ± 10% (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: After treating MV4;11 cells with 100 nM pinometostat for 7 days, there was no discernable effect on the expression of HOXA9 and MEIS1.
source: Notably, after treating MV4;11 cells with 100 nM inhibitor for 7 days we observed no discernable effect on the expression of HOXA9 and MEIS1 (Figure 1D and E), despite the emphasis on these genes as the critical mediators of DOT1L's effects in MLL-r leukemia (Okada et al., 2005; Bernt et al., 2011; Guenther et al., 2008; Daigle et al., 2011; Deshpande et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: Treatment with 1 µM pinometostat significantly downregulates both HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression.
source: Consistent with prior observations (Daigle et al., 2013), a much higher dose of 1 µM pinometostat significantly downregulates both HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Treatment with SGC0946, a distinct DOT1L inhibitor, also reduced MV4;11 proliferation without affecting HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression.
source: Treatment with a low-dose regime of SGC0946, a distinct, yet highly selective DOT1L inhibitor (Yu et al., 2012) also reduced MV4;11 proliferation without affecting HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments with a different DOT1L inhibitor shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment for 7 days resulted in 1916 genes downregulated and 2007 genes upregulated in MV4;11 cells.
source: To define these genes, we performed RNA-seq in MV4;11 cells that had been treated with 100 nM pinometostat for 7 days and observed that 1916 genes were downregulated and 2007 genes were upregulated (Figure 2A) relative to a DMSO treated control.
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The downregulated genes significantly overlap with MLL-AF4 targets identified by Kerry et al. by ChIP-seq in MV4;11 cells.
source: The downregulated genes significantly overlap with MLL-AF4 targets identified by Kerry et al. by ChIP-seq in MV4;11 cells (Kerry et al., 2017; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from comparison of RNA-seq data with published ChIP-seq data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There is marked overlap between genes downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat and genes downregulated by 3 µM EPZ004777.
source: Relative to prior high-dose (3 µM) treatment with a compound structurally related to pinometostat in MV4;11 cells, the numbers of differentially expressed genes are similar, and there is marked overlap between the sets, particularly the downregulated cohort (Daigle et al., 2011; Figure 2C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from comparison with published data, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: HOXA9 expression was unaltered by 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Consistent with our RT-qPCR measurements, HOXA9 was unaltered in its expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) and MEIS1 displayed extremely modest mRNA reduction (20%) not observed by RT-qPCR and not reflected in apparent protein levels (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: MEIS1 displayed extremely modest mRNA reduction (20%) by RNA-seq that was not observed by RT-qPCR and not reflected in apparent protein levels.
source: Consistent with our RT-qPCR measurements, HOXA9 was unaltered in its expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) and MEIS1 displayed extremely modest mRNA reduction (20%) not observed by RT-qPCR and not reflected in apparent protein levels (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is a finding comparing RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and Western blot data.

claim: Of the HOXA cluster genes, only HOXA11 and HOXA13 exhibited expression changes with 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Of the other HOXA cluster genes only HOXA11 and HOXA13 exhibited expression changes with a 1.7-fold decrease and 2.5-fold increase, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: HOXA11 expression decreased 1.7-fold with 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Of the other HOXA cluster genes only HOXA11 and HOXA13 exhibited expression changes with a 1.7-fold decrease and 2.5-fold increase, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: HOXA13 expression increased 2.5-fold with 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Of the other HOXA cluster genes only HOXA11 and HOXA13 exhibited expression changes with a 1.7-fold decrease and 2.5-fold increase, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: 906 genes were upregulated at least twofold by 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Although H3K79me2 is considered transcriptionally activating, the upregulated genes had much larger expression fold-changes. 906 genes were upregulated at least twofold (and some > 80-fold), while only 86 genes were downregulated ≥ 2-fold (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Only 86 genes were downregulated ≥ 2-fold by 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Although H3K79me2 is considered transcriptionally activating, the upregulated genes had much larger expression fold-changes. 906 genes were upregulated at least twofold (and some > 80-fold), while only 86 genes were downregulated ≥ 2-fold (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The list of upregulated transcripts includes MHC class II and innate immune response genes.
source: The list of upregulated transcripts includes MHC class II and innate immune response genes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment increased expression of CIITA, HLA-DRA and HLA-DRB1.
source: We confirmed the expression increases of CIITA (the master regulator of interferon-inducible MHC class II genes), and the MHC class II genes HLA-DRA and HLA-DRB1 by RT-qPCR (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of the upregulated genes indicated enrichment for 'immune response' and 'interferon-gamma signaling pathway'.
source: Gene ontology analysis of the upregulated genes indicated enrichment for 'immune response' and 'interferon-gamma signaling pathway' (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Huang et al., 2009a; Huang et al., 2009b).
evidence: This is a finding from gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was no discernable effect on interferon-gamma (IFNG) expression in the RNA-seq analysis.
source: Despite there being no discernable effect on interferon-gamma (IFNG) expression in the RNA-seq analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), marked activation of IFN-γ-inducible genes is apparent.
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Marked activation of IFN-γ-inducible genes is apparent despite no change in IFNG expression.
source: Despite there being no discernable effect on interferon-gamma (IFNG) expression in the RNA-seq analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), marked activation of IFN-γ-inducible genes is apparent.
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data.

claim: The activation of IFN-γ-inducible genes may be due to perturbations to signaling effectors of the IFN-γ pathway including the STAT family of transcription factors.
source: We hypothesize that this may be due to perturbations to signaling effectors of the IFN-γ pathway which includes the STAT family of transcription factors that are often aberrantly expressed in leukemia and other cancers (Caldarelli et al., 2013; Spiekermann et al., 2002; Muhlethaler-Mottet et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their data and cited literature.

claim: STAT family transcription factors are often aberrantly expressed in leukemia and other cancers.
source: We hypothesize that this may be due to perturbations to signaling effectors of the IFN-γ pathway which includes the STAT family of transcription factors that are often aberrantly expressed in leukemia and other cancers (Caldarelli et al., 2013; Spiekermann et al., 2002; Muhlethaler-Mottet et al., 1998).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The activation of genes involved in antigen processing and presentation and macrophage cell surface markers may indicate that MV4;11 cells are undergoing differentiation toward a more macrophage-like state.
source: The activation of so many genes involved in antigen processing and presentation as well as macrophage cell surface markers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C) may indicate that these cells are undergoing differentiation toward a more macrophage-like state, consistent with apparent differentiation observed in other DOT1L loss-of-function paradigms (Bernt et al., 2011; Daigle et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference from RNA-seq data and comparison with cited literature.

claim: By GSEA, the set of differentially expressed genes were enriched for hematopoietic differentiation factors and anticorrelated with hematopoietic progenitor expression signatures.
source: By Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) (Subramanian et al., 2005; Mootha et al., 2003), the set of differentially expressed genes were enriched for hematopoietic differentiation factors and anticorrelated with hematopoietic progenitor expression signatures (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The cytokine receptors CSF1R and CSF3R were upregulated by 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: Notably, the cytokine receptors CSF1R and CSF3R, critical signaling inducers of hematopoietic differentiation, were upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E; Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013; Klimiankou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: CSF1R and CSF3R are critical signaling inducers of hematopoietic differentiation.
source: Notably, the cytokine receptors CSF1R and CSF3R, critical signaling inducers of hematopoietic differentiation, were upregulated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E; Mossadegh-Keller et al., 2013; Klimiankou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Among the most downregulated genes were many MLL-AF4 target genes including FLT3, MEF2C, and PBX3.
source: Among the most downregulated genes were many MLL-AF4 target genes (Kerry et al., 2017; Guenther et al., 2008; Wilkinson et al., 2013) including the oncogene FMS-Like Tyrosine Kinase 3 (FLT3), the protooncogene Myocyte Enhancer Factor 2C (MEF2C), and Pre-B-cell leukemia homeobox 3 (PBX3) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: FLT3, MEF2C, and PBX3 all have previously described roles in the development of MLL-rearranged leukemias.
source: These genes all have previously described roles in the development of MLL-rearranged leukemias (Stubbs et al., 2008; Nagel et al., 2017; Krivtsov et al., 2006; Li et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: FLT3 is a receptor tyrosine kinase that regulates proliferation and cell survival via STAT and other signaling pathways.
source: FLT3 is a receptor tyrosine kinase that regulates proliferation and cell survival via STAT and other signaling pathways.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about FLT3.

claim: Mutations that constitutively activate FLT3 by internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) or point mutations within its kinase domain collectively represent the most frequently occurring genetic lesions in acute myeloid leukemia.
source: Mutations that constitutively activate FLT3 by internal tandem duplication of its juxtamembrane domain (FLT3-ITD) or point mutations within its kinase domain collectively represent the most frequently occuring genetic lesions in acute myeloid leukemia (Nagel et al., 2017; Levis and Small, 2003; Mizuki et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MV4;11 cells are homozygous for the FLT3-ITD mutation.
source: MV4;11 cells are homozygous for the FLT3-ITD mutation and highly sensitive to FLT3 inhibition (Armstrong et al., 2003; Levis et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MV4;11 cells are highly sensitive to FLT3 inhibition.
source: MV4;11 cells are homozygous for the FLT3-ITD mutation and highly sensitive to FLT3 inhibition (Armstrong et al., 2003; Levis et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MEF2C cooperates with SOX4 to induce leukemogenesis in mouse models.
source: The transcription factor MEF2C cooperates with SOX4 to induce leukemogenesis in mouse models and MLL-AF9-expressing hematopoietic progenitors to promote colony formation (Krivtsov et al., 2006; Du et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MEF2C promotes colony formation in MLL-AF9-expressing hematopoietic progenitors.
source: The transcription factor MEF2C cooperates with SOX4 to induce leukemogenesis in mouse models and MLL-AF9-expressing hematopoietic progenitors to promote colony formation (Krivtsov et al., 2006; Du et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: PBX3 is a transcription factor that acts to stabilize both HOXA9 and MEIS1 localization at a subset of target genes.
source: PBX3 is a transcription factor that acts to stabilize both HOXA9 and MEIS1 localization at a subset of target genes and coexpression of either oncogene with PBX3 can cause leukemogenesis (Li et al., 2016; Li et al., 2013b; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Coexpression of either HOXA9 or MEIS1 with PBX3 can cause leukemogenesis.
source: PBX3 is a transcription factor that acts to stabilize both HOXA9 and MEIS1 localization at a subset of target genes and coexpression of either oncogene with PBX3 can cause leukemogenesis (Li et al., 2016; Li et al., 2013b; Wang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment reduced FLT3, MEF2C and PBX3 expression as verified by RT-qPCR.
source: We verified the reductions in FLT3, MEF2C and PBX3 expression with pinometostat by RT-qPCR and examined FLT3 protein levels by Western blot (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment reduced FLT3 protein levels as shown by Western blot.
source: We verified the reductions in FLT3, MEF2C and PBX3 expression with pinometostat by RT-qPCR and examined FLT3 protein levels by Western blot (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Of 15 genes downregulated by MEF2C knockout in mouse hematopoietic progenitors, only FLT3 was downregulated in pinometostat-treated MV4;11 cells.
source: Using previously published datasets of MEF2C and FLT3-regulated genes, we first looked at the expression of 15 genes that were downregulated by MEF2C knockout in mouse hematopoietic progenitors (Stehling-Sun et al., 2009). Of these genes, only FLT3 was downregulated in our pinometostat-treated cells.
evidence: This is a finding from comparison of RNA-seq data with published datasets.

claim: There is a small but significant overlap between genes upregulated in FLT3-ITD+ AML and genes downregulated by pinometostat.
source: Previous work by Cauchy et al. identified 138 genes significantly upregulated in karyotypically normal FLT3-ITD+ AML compared to WT FLT3 AML patient samples (Cauchy et al., 2015). A comparison of those FLT3-ITD-upregulated genes to our pinomeostat downregulated genes yielded a small but significant overlap (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a finding from comparison with published patient data, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: There is a more pronounced overlap between genes downregulated in FLT3-ITD+ patient samples and those upregulated by pinometostat, including 10 MHC class II receptors.
source: We saw a more pronounced overlap between genes downregulated in FLT3-ITD+ patient samples and those upregulated by pinometostat, including 10 MHC class II receptors (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is a finding from comparison with published patient data, shown in Figure 2I.

claim: PBX3 is the only MLL-AF4 target upregulated in FLT3-ITD patient samples.
source: PBX3 is the only MLL-AF4 target upregulated in the FLT3-ITD samples, suggesting it could be a crucial convergence point of the MLL-AF4 and FLT3-ITD pathways.
evidence: This is a finding from comparison with published patient data.

claim: PBX3 could be a crucial convergence point of the MLL-AF4 and FLT3-ITD pathways.
source: PBX3 is the only MLL-AF4 target upregulated in the FLT3-ITD samples, suggesting it could be a crucial convergence point of the MLL-AF4 and FLT3-ITD pathways.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: ICeChIP measured a positive correlation (R2 = 0.53) between transcript abundance and H3K79me2 levels in MV4;11 cells.
source: With ICeChIP we were able to measure a positive correlation (R2 = 0.53) between transcript abundance and H3K79me2 levels in MV4;11 cells (Figure 3A), consistent with the speculated role for H3K79me2 in transcriptional activation (Okada et al., 2005; Bernt et al., 2011; Chen et al., 2015a; Daigle et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Only 30 of the 250 most highly expressed genes were downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: However, only 30 of the 250 most highly expressed genes, were downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat treatment, suggesting that H3K79me2 is not necessary to maintain high levels of gene expression at all sites where it is enriched.
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: H3K79me2 is not necessary to maintain high levels of gene expression at all sites where it is enriched.
source: However, only 30 of the 250 most highly expressed genes, were downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat treatment, suggesting that H3K79me2 is not necessary to maintain high levels of gene expression at all sites where it is enriched.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: Genes downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat had higher H3K79me2 levels compared to upregulated genes or all expressed genes.
source: The genes that were downregulated by 100 nM pinomeostat had higher H3K79me2 levels compared to upregulated genes or all expressed genes, rivalling the most highly expressed genes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: MLL-AF4 targets have equivalent average H3K79me2 density to the 250 most highly expressed genes.
source: Although previous conventional ChIP-seq measurements observed enrichment of H3K79me2 at MLL-fusion target genes (Bernt et al., 2011; Guenther et al., 2008), our ICe-ChIP-seq analysis revealed equivalent average density at MLL-AF4 targets and the 250 most highly expressed genes (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The higher H3K79me2 density at MLL-AF4 targets is likely due to very efficient recruitment of DOT1L by MLL-AF4 rather than deposition via the transcriptional apparatus.
source: Given that only 12 MLL-AF4 targets are included in that highly expressed gene list, this higher H3K79me2 density is likely due to very efficient recruitment of DOT1L by MLL-AF4 rather than deposition via the transcriptional apparatus (Schübeler et al., 2004; Guenther et al., 2007).
evidence: This is an inference from the data and cited literature.

claim: The subset of MLL-AF4 targets that are downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat exhibit higher levels of H3K79me2 than MLL-AF4 targets as a whole.
source: Interestingly, the subset of MLL-AF4 targets that are downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat exhibit still higher levels of H3K79me2 than even MLL-AF4 targets as a whole and appear to be more dependent on H3K79me2 for their expression (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: MLL-AF4 targets downregulated by pinometostat appear to be more dependent on H3K79me2 for their expression.
source: Interestingly, the subset of MLL-AF4 targets that are downregulated by 100 nM pinometostat exhibit still higher levels of H3K79me2 than even MLL-AF4 targets as a whole and appear to be more dependent on H3K79me2 for their expression (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is an inference from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: MLL-spreading genes have peak H3K79me2 levels comparable to pinometostat-downregulated MLL-AF4 targets.
source: The only other group of genes analyzed with comparable peak H3K79me2 levels were 'MLL-spreading' genes which display a binding profile that stretches further downstream into the gene body (Kerry et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat dramatically reduced H3K79me2 density in gene bodies across all gene categories examined.
source: In all gene categories we examined, 100 nM pinometostat dramatically reduced apparent H3K79me2 density in gene bodies, eliminating the sharp peaks near the TSS and proportionally reducing methylation as it tapers toward the 3' end of the gene body (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Pinometostat treatment eliminated the sharp H3K79me2 peaks near the TSS.
source: In all gene categories we examined, 100 nM pinometostat dramatically reduced apparent H3K79me2 density in gene bodies, eliminating the sharp peaks near the TSS and proportionally reducing methylation as it tapers toward the 3' end of the gene body (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The upregulated gene set displayed lower-than-average H3K79me2 density both before and after pinometostat treatment.
source: The upregulated gene set displayed lower-than-average density both before and after treatment, consistent with the transcriptional upregulation occurring as an indirect effect of the dosing.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: The similar reductions in H3K79me2 methylation at gene groups with different responses to pinometostat suggest that the expression of some genes is more dependent on H3K79me2-mediated transcriptional activation.
source: The similar reductions in methylation at gene groups that had such different overall responses to gene expression from pinometostat treatment suggests that the expression of some genes is more dependent on H3K79me2-mediated transcriptional activation.
evidence: This is an inference from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: There is an unexpectedly poor linear correlation (R2 = 0.13) between fold-change in H3K79me2 HMD versus fold-change in gene expression of differentially expressed genes.
source: Given the modest correlation between H3K79me2 early in the gene body and transcriptional output, we observed an unexpectedly poor linear correlation between fold-change in H3K79me2 HMD versus fold-change in gene expression of differentially expressed genes (R2 = 0.13) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq and RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Genes with the largest reductions in H3K79me2 HMD are nearly uniformly downregulated though not in proportion to HMD loss.
source: However, comparing the absolute differences in HMD to fold-change of gene expression more clearly reveals some interesting trends (Figure 3C). Those genes with the largest reductions in HMD (including MLL-AF4 targets) are nearly uniformly downregulated though not in proportion to HMD loss.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq and RNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MLL-AF4 targets with smaller HMD reductions are more evenly distributed between both up- and downregulated genes.
source: Conversely, MLL-AF4 targets with smaller HMD reductions are more evenly distributed between both up- and downregulated genes.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq and RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: FLT3-ITD-upregulated genes have only small reductions in H3K79me2 HMD, suggesting their downregulation is not a direct result of HMD loss but a secondary effect of FLT3 downregulation.
source: FLT3-ITD-upregulated genes identified in patient samples (Cauchy et al., 2015) have only small reductions in HMD, suggesting their downregulation is not a direct result of HMD loss but, instead, a secondary effect of FLT3 downregulation.
evidence: This is an inference from ICeChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: The MLL-AF4 targets downregulated by low-dose pinometostat had the largest reductions in H3K79me2 of any gene category examined.
source: Interestingly, the MLL-AF4 targets downregulated by low-dose pinometostat (Figure 2B) had the largest reductions in H3K79me2 of any gene category examined (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A subset of MLL-AF4 targets have higher levels of H3K79me2 and greater reductions from DOT1L inhibition and are more dependent on this methylation for expression.
source: These data show that a subset of MLL-AF4 targets have higher levels of H3K79me2 and greater reductions from DOT1L inhibition and are more dependent on this methylation for even moderate levels of expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion from ICeChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Gene expression sensitivity to low-dose DOT1L inhibition may more accurately define 'true' MLL-AF4 target genes than those genes that merely align with MLL1 and AF4 ChIP-seq peaks.
source: Gene expression sensitivity to low-dose DOT1L inhibition may more accurately define 'true' MLL-AF4 target genes whose expression is upregulated by the fusion protein and H3K79me2 hypermethylation than those genes that merely align with MLL1 and AF4 ChIP-seq peaks.
evidence: This is an inference from the study's findings.

claim: Treating MV4;11 cells with 100 nM pinometostat for 4 days had little effect on H3K79me2 HMD at the most highly expressed genes.
source: To further define the H3K79me2 depletion trajectory, we also examined the distribution of this modification within gene bodies at an earlier timepoint of pinometostat treatment. Treating MV4;11 cells with 100 nM pinometostat for 4 days had little effect on H3K79me2 HMD at the most highly expressed genes, which likely depend more on DOT1L recruitment by the transcriptional apparatus than by the MLL-fusion protein (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pinometostat treatment for 4 days diminished the 5' H3K79me2 peak at genes downregulated by 7-day pinometostat treatment and at MLL-AF4 targets.
source: Pinometostat treatment for 4 days diminished the 5' H3K79me2 peak at genes downregulated by 7-day pinometostat treatment and at MLL-AF4 targets while only slightly reducing H3K79me2 levels within gene bodies of MLL-AF4 targets.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: Within the gene bodies of 100 nM (7 day) pinometostat-downregulated genes there was an increase in H3K79me2 HMD at the 4-day timepoint.
source: Within the gene bodies of 100 nM (7 day) pinometostat-downregulated genes there was actually an increase in H3K79me2 HMD at the 4-day timepoint.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: The 3' shift in H3K79me2 methylation density away from the transcription start site was even more evident in 'MLL-spreading' genes.
source: This 3' shift in methylation density away from the transcription start site was even more evident in 'MLL-spreading' genes, which showed little reduction in peak methylation levels seen in other groups.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: The absence of correlation between H3K79me2 loss and reductions in gene expression suggests that this modification does not have a universal and proportionate effect on gene activation.
source: The absence of correlation between H3K79me2 loss and reductions in gene expression suggests that this modification does not have a universal and proportionate effect on gene activation.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: Some MLL-AF4 targets have higher levels of H3K79me2 and are more sensitive to its depletion.
source: Rather, it appears some MLL-AF4 targets have higher levels of H3K79me2 and are more sensitive to its depletion.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the data.

claim: Higher H3K79me2 methylation levels may result in greater dependence on this modification for gene expression at a subset of MLL-AF4 targets.
source: It is possible that the higher methylation levels result in greater dependence on this modification for gene expression at a subset of MLL-AF4 targets.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data.

claim: When comparing MLL-r cell lines with the same MLL-translocation, those with the FLT3-ITD mutation were significantly more sensitive to 100 nM pinometostat than those with normal FLT3 alleles.
source: We treated all four cell lines with 100 nM pinometostat for 7 days. When comparing each cell line to its counterpart with the same MLL-translocation, those with the FLT3-ITD mutation were significantly more sensitive to DOT1L inhibition than those with normal FLT3 alleles (Figure 4A, left).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: After 7 days of 100 nM pinometostat treatment MV4;11 viability was reduced by 74 ± 3%.
source: After 7 days of 100 nM pinometostat treatment MV4;11 viability was drastically reduced by 74 ± 3% while the viability of SEM, its MLL-AF4 counterpart with intact FLT3, was unaltered within experimental error.
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays.

claim: The viability of SEM cells (MLL-AF4, intact FLT3) was unaltered by 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: After 7 days of 100 nM pinometostat treatment MV4;11 viability was drastically reduced by 74 ± 3% while the viability of SEM, its MLL-AF4 counterpart with intact FLT3, was unaltered within experimental error.
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays.

claim: MOLM13 viability was reduced by 21 ± 3% after 7 days of 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: MOLM13 viability was somewhat reduced (21 ± 3%) while there was no significant difference in the viability of THP-1 cells.
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays.

claim: There was no significant difference in the viability of THP-1 cells after 100 nM pinometostat treatment.
source: MOLM13 viability was somewhat reduced (21 ± 3%) while there was no significant difference in the viability of THP-1 cells.
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays.

claim: MOLM13 cells displayed no change in HOXA9 or MEIS1 expression under 100 nM pinometostat treatment conditions.
source: As in MV4;11 cells, MOLM13 cells displayed no change in HOXA9 or MEIS1 expression under these conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cell lines with FLT3-ITD mutations were significantly more sensitive to 30 nM tandutinib (FLT3 inhibitor) than those with wild type FLT3.
source: The small molecule tandutinib (MLN518) inhibits FLT3 kinase activity, severely reducing phosphorylation-mediated activation of downstream targets such as STAT5A (Clark et al., 2004). We treated our MLL-r cell lines with 30 nM tandutinib for 7 days. As with the DOT1L inhibition experiments, cell lines with FLT3-ITD mutations were significantly more susceptible to the inhibitor's effects (Figure 4A, right).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Tandutinib (MLN518) inhibits FLT3 kinase activity, severely reducing phosphorylation-mediated activation of downstream targets such as STAT5A.
source: The small molecule tandutinib (MLN518) inhibits FLT3 kinase activity, severely reducing phosphorylation-mediated activation of downstream targets such as STAT5A (Clark et al., 2004).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The FLT3-ITD mutation allows FLT3 to phosphorylate STAT5A, a transcription factor that is not activated by wild type FLT3.
source: The FLT3-ITD mutation allows FLT3 to phosphorylate STAT5A, a transcription factor that is not activated by wild type FLT3 (Choudhary et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: STAT5A phosphorylation licenses translocation to the nucleus to drive target gene transcription, resulting in a hyperproliferative state necessary for leukemia cell survival.
source: This aberrant STAT5A phosphorylation licenses translocation to the nucleus to drive target gene transcription, resulting in a hyperproliferative state necessary for leukemia cell survival (Onishi et al., 1998; Choudhary et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat treatment for 7 days reduced STAT5A phosphorylation in MV4;11 cells without affecting STAT5A protein levels.
source: We hypothesized that FLT3-ITD downregulation by DOT1L inhibition would thereby reduce STAT5A phosphorylation. Indeed, 100 nM pinometostat as well as SGC0946 treatment for 7 days reduced STAT5A phosphorylation in MV4;11 cells without affecting STAT5A protein levels (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), where pinometostat reduced STAT5A phosphorylation by 65 ± 8% (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pinometostat reduced STAT5A phosphorylation by 65 ± 8% in MV4;11 cells.
source: We hypothesized that FLT3-ITD downregulation by DOT1L inhibition would thereby reduce STAT5A phosphorylation. Indeed, 100 nM pinometostat as well as SGC0946 treatment for 7 days reduced STAT5A phosphorylation in MV4;11 cells without affecting STAT5A protein levels (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), where pinometostat reduced STAT5A phosphorylation by 65 ± 8% (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from quantitative Western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Pinometostat treatment slightly reduced STAT5 phosphorylation in MOLM13 cells.
source: We observed that pinometostat treatment slightly reduced STAT5 phosphorylation in MOLM13 cells, consistent with the lower FLT3-ITD allele dose, whereas lines with wild type FLT3 (THP-1, SEM) did not display these effects.
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data.

claim: Cell lines with wild type FLT3 (THP-1, SEM) did not display reduced STAT5 phosphorylation with pinometostat treatment.
source: We observed that pinometostat treatment slightly reduced STAT5 phosphorylation in MOLM13 cells, consistent with the lower FLT3-ITD allele dose, whereas lines with wild type FLT3 (THP-1, SEM) did not display these effects.
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data.

claim: Small molecule inhibition of FLT3 signaling yielded markedly reduced STAT5 phosphorylation in lines bearing the FLT3-ITD (MV4;11 and MOLM13).
source: As a point of direct comparison, small molecule inhibition of FLT3 signaling yielded markedly reduced STAT5 phosphorylation in lines bearing the FLT3-ITD (MV4;11 and MOLM13), with a more modest reduction in SEM cells while phospho-STAT5 was barely detectable in THP-1 cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: FLT3 expression was significantly reduced 48 hr after pinometostat treatment.
source: To examine whether FLT3 effects precede other pro-proliferation pathways, we obtained more granular expression kinetics of several downregulated MLL-AF4 targets that have been implicated in leukemogenesis. Expression of FLT3, PBX3, PIM1 and MEF2C was significantly reduced after 72 hr treatment with pinometostat (Figure 4C), however, FLT3 was the only gene whose expression was reduced 48 hr after treatment, suggesting it is more sensitive to H3K79me2 reductions than the others examined.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR time course data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: FLT3 was the only gene whose expression was reduced 48 hr after pinometostat treatment, suggesting it is more sensitive to H3K79me2 reductions.
source: To examine whether FLT3 effects precede other pro-proliferation pathways, we obtained more granular expression kinetics of several downregulated MLL-AF4 targets that have been implicated in leukemogenesis. Expression of FLT3, PBX3, PIM1 and MEF2C was significantly reduced after 72 hr treatment with pinometostat (Figure 4C), however, FLT3 was the only gene whose expression was reduced 48 hr after treatment, suggesting it is more sensitive to H3K79me2 reductions than the others examined.
evidence: This is a finding and inference from RT-qPCR time course data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression of FLT3, PBX3, PIM1 and MEF2C was significantly reduced after 72 hr treatment with pinometostat.
source: To examine whether FLT3 effects precede other pro-proliferation pathways, we obtained more granular expression kinetics of several downregulated MLL-AF4 targets that have been implicated in leukemogenesis. Expression of FLT3, PBX3, PIM1 and MEF2C was significantly reduced after 72 hr treatment with pinometostat (Figure 4C), however, FLT3 was the only gene whose expression was reduced 48 hr after treatment, suggesting it is more sensitive to H3K79me2 reductions than the others examined.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR time course data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: FLT3 and MEF2C are targets of the HOXA9-MEIS1-PBX3 complex.
source: Though FLT3 and MEF2C are targets of the HOXA9-MEIS1-PBX3 complex, these genes are all targets of the MLL-fusion protein (Kerry et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: FLT3, PBX3, PIM1 and MEF2C are all targets of the MLL-fusion protein.
source: Though FLT3 and MEF2C are targets of the HOXA9-MEIS1-PBX3 complex, these genes are all targets of the MLL-fusion protein (Kerry et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The reduction in FLT3 expression in advance of decreased PBX3 or MEF2C expression suggests that DOT1L inhibition directly affects FLT3 gene expression independently of PBX3 or MEF2C.
source: The reduction in FLT3 expression in advance of decreased PBX3 or MEF2C expression lends tentative support to the possibility that DOT1L inhibition directly affects FLT3 gene expression independently of PBX3 or MEF2C.
evidence: This is an inference from the time course data.

claim: GSEA of pinometostat-downregulated genes and genes upregulated by STAT5A overexpression showed a negative correlation (NES = −1.87, FDR = 0.003).
source: We performed GSEA (Subramanian et al., 2005; Mootha et al., 2003) with the pinometostat-downregulated genes and genes upregulated by STAT5A overexpression in human CD34+ hematopoietic progenitors (Wierenga et al., 2008) and observed a negative correlation indicative of significant pathway overlap (NES = −1.87, FDR = 0.003, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: PIM1 and ARID3B are STAT5A target genes downregulated by pinometostat.
source: We then reexamined our RNA-seq data for previously described STAT5A target genes downregulated by pinometostat and found several, including PIM1 and ARID3B (Kim et al., 2005; Ribeiro et al., 2018; Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The PIM proteins are a family of 3 protooncogene serine/tyrosine kinases (PIM1-3) that are upregulated in leukemia, prostate, mesothelioma and other cancers.
source: The PIM proteins are a family of 3 protooncogene serine/tyrosine kinases (PIM1-3) that are upregulated in, and indicative of poor prognosis in leukemia, prostate, mesothelioma and other cancers (Mizuki et al., 2003; Kim et al., 2005; Amson et al., 1989; Cibull et al., 2006; Peltola et al., 2009; Deneen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Only PIM1 and PIM2 expression is increased in FLT3 inhibitor-resistant FLT3-ITD patient samples.
source: However, only PIM1 and PIM2 expression is increased in FLT3 inhibitor-resistant FLT3-ITD patient samples and exogenous expression of either PIM1 or PIM2 can rescue proliferation defects caused by loss of FLT3 activity in MOLM14 cells (MLL-AF9, FLT3-ITD heterozygous) (Adam et al., 2006; Green et al., 2015; Fathi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Exogenous expression of either PIM1 or PIM2 can rescue proliferation defects caused by loss of FLT3 activity in MOLM14 cells.
source: However, only PIM1 and PIM2 expression is increased in FLT3 inhibitor-resistant FLT3-ITD patient samples and exogenous expression of either PIM1 or PIM2 can rescue proliferation defects caused by loss of FLT3 activity in MOLM14 cells (MLL-AF9, FLT3-ITD heterozygous) (Adam et al., 2006; Green et al., 2015; Fathi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: PIM1 and PIM2 are both downregulated in the RNA-seq analysis of pinometostat-treated cells.
source: Although PIM1 and PIM2 are both downregulated in our RNA-seq analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), we observed a much greater reduction in PIM1 expression by RT-qPCR (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: A much greater reduction in PIM1 expression was observed by RT-qPCR compared to PIM2.
source: Although PIM1 and PIM2 are both downregulated in our RNA-seq analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E), we observed a much greater reduction in PIM1 expression by RT-qPCR (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Treating MV4;11 cells with tandutinib (FLT3 inhibitor) resulted in downregulation of PIM1, ARID3B, and PBX3 but not PIM2.
source: Treating MV4;11 cells with tandutinib (FLT3 inhibitor) resulted in downregulation of PIM1, ARID3B, and PBX3 but not PIM2 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Treating MOLM13 cells with pinometostat reduced expression of MEF2C, FLT3 and PIM1, but caused no change in PBX3 expression.
source: Treating MOLM13 cells with pinometostat also reduced expression of MEF2C, FLT3 and PIM1, but caused no change in PBX3 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: FLT3 knockdown reduces MV4;11 proliferation.
source: With modest knockdown of FLT3 (Figure 4G), we observed significant reductions in the proliferation of three different clonal lines as compared to a scrambled shRNA (Figure 4F). FLT3 knockdown reduces MV4;11 proliferation and STAT5A phosphorylation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I), analogous to the effects of pinometostat treatment.
evidence: This is a finding from shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: FLT3 knockdown reduces STAT5A phosphorylation in MV4;11 cells.
source: With modest knockdown of FLT3 (Figure 4G), we observed significant reductions in the proliferation of three different clonal lines as compared to a scrambled shRNA (Figure 4F). FLT3 knockdown reduces MV4;11 proliferation and STAT5A phosphorylation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I), analogous to the effects of pinometostat treatment.
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I.

claim: FLT3 knockdown significantly reduced the expression of the STAT5A target genes PIM1 and ARID3B.
source: Akin to the DOT1L and FLT3 inhibitors (Figure 4D–E), FLT3 knockdown also significantly reduced the expression of the STAT5A target genes PIM1 and ARID3B, with PIM2 expression reduced in only 1 of 3 clones (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: PIM2 expression was reduced in only 1 of 3 FLT3 knockdown clones.
source: Akin to the DOT1L and FLT3 inhibitors (Figure 4D–E), FLT3 knockdown also significantly reduced the expression of the STAT5A target genes PIM1 and ARID3B, with PIM2 expression reduced in only 1 of 3 clones (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Other kinases such as JAK1-3 or TYK2 may also activate STAT5A in MV4;11 cells.
source: We observe more modest reduction in STAT5A signaling upon FLT3-ITD knockdown compared to pinometostat treatment, perhaps indicating that other kinases such as JAK1-3 or TYK2, with previously observed roles in STAT5A activation, may also activate STAT5A in this context and further, that the function of one or more of these other kinases may also be reduced by pinometostat treatment (Paukku and Silvennoinen, 2004).
evidence: This is speculation based on the data and cited literature.

claim: FLT3 knockdown resulted in PBX3 downregulation, suggesting that FLT3 can regulate the expression of this oncogenic transcription factor.
source: Interestingly, FLT3 knockdown also resulted in PBX3 downregulation, suggesting that FLT3 can regulate the expression of this oncogenic transcription factor, in line with previous observations (Cauchy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding and inference from the data, consistent with cited literature.

claim: DOT1L inhibitors may act, in part, by disrupting FLT3 signaling culminating in a reduction in STAT5A target expression and function.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that the DOT1L inhibitors may act, in part, by disrupting FLT3 signaling culminating in a reduction in STAT5A target expression and function.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's data.

claim: 10 µM pinometostat reduced the viability of the FLT3-ITD heterozygous, non-MLL-rearranged leukemia cell line PL-21 after treatment for 9 days.
source: We observed a reduction in the viability of the FLT3-ITD heterozygous, non-MLL-rearranged leukemia cell line PL-21 after treatment with 10 µM pinometostat for 9 days (Figure 4H), accompanied by a reduction in both FLT3 and PIM1 expression (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 4H.

claim: 10 µM pinometostat treatment of PL-21 cells was accompanied by a reduction in both FLT3 and PIM1 expression.
source: We observed a reduction in the viability of the FLT3-ITD heterozygous, non-MLL-rearranged leukemia cell line PL-21 after treatment with 10 µM pinometostat for 9 days (Figure 4H), accompanied by a reduction in both FLT3 and PIM1 expression (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: The viability of K562 cells was not affected after treatment with 10 µM pinometostat for 11 days.
source: Whereas the viability of K562 cells, an erythroleukemic cell line with a BCR-ABL translocation was not affected after treatment with 10 µM pinometostat for 11 days.
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays.

claim: 9 days pinometostat treatment of PL-21 cells resulted in reductions in H3K79me2 and STAT5A phosphorylation.
source: We observed reductions in H3K79me2 and STAT5A phosphorylation after 9 days pinometostat treatment, suggesting that DOT1L inhibition may also reduce the viability of non-MLL-rearranged FLT-ITD leukemias through disruption of FLT3-ITD/STAT5A signaling (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: DOT1L inhibition may reduce the viability of non-MLL-rearranged FLT3-ITD leukemias through disruption of FLT3-ITD/STAT5A signaling.
source: We observed reductions in H3K79me2 and STAT5A phosphorylation after 9 days pinometostat treatment, suggesting that DOT1L inhibition may also reduce the viability of non-MLL-rearranged FLT-ITD leukemias through disruption of FLT3-ITD/STAT5A signaling (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression were not detectable by RT-qPCR in PL-21 cells.
source: Furthermore, expression of the MLL-r leukemic drivers HOXA9 and MEIS1 were not detectable by RT-qPCR in PL-21 cells (Figure 4I), arguing that FLT3-ITD targeting by pinometostat is completely distinct.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: FLT3-ITD targeting by pinometostat is completely distinct from HOXA9/MEIS1 pathways in PL-21 cells.
source: Furthermore, expression of the MLL-r leukemic drivers HOXA9 and MEIS1 were not detectable by RT-qPCR in PL-21 cells (Figure 4I), arguing that FLT3-ITD targeting by pinometostat is completely distinct.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: DOT1L inhibition in leukemia cell lines with MLL1 partial tandem duplications (MLL-PTD) reduced cell viability, downregulated MLL1 target genes including HOXA9 and induced apoptosis and differentiation.
source: In a previous study, DOT1L inhibition in leukemia cell lines with MLL1 partial tandem duplications (MLL-PTD) reduced cell viability, downregulated MLL1 target genes including HOXA9 and induced apoptosis and differentiation (Kühn et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: 10 µM pinometostat reduced EOL-1 proliferation and HOXA9 expression.
source: We recapitulate these findings with 10 µM pinometostat reduced EOL-1 (MLL-PTD, intact FLT3) proliferation and HOXA9 expression, noting also reductions in FLT3 and PIM1 expression but no change in MEIS1 expression (Figure 4H,K).
evidence: This is a finding from experiments shown in Figures 4H and 4K.

claim: 10 µM pinometostat treatment of EOL-1 cells resulted in reductions in FLT3 and PIM1 expression but no change in MEIS1 expression.
source: We recapitulate these findings with 10 µM pinometostat reduced EOL-1 (MLL-PTD, intact FLT3) proliferation and HOXA9 expression, noting also reductions in FLT3 and PIM1 expression but no change in MEIS1 expression (Figure 4H,K).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat reduced EOL-1 viability.
source: Surprisingly, a 10-fold lower dose of pinometostat also reduced EOL-1 viability (Figure 4H) and FLT3 expression with no discernable changes in HOXA9, MEIS1 or PIM1 expression (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 4H.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat reduced FLT3 expression in EOL-1 cells with no discernable changes in HOXA9, MEIS1 or PIM1 expression.
source: Surprisingly, a 10-fold lower dose of pinometostat also reduced EOL-1 viability (Figure 4H) and FLT3 expression with no discernable changes in HOXA9, MEIS1 or PIM1 expression (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Low-dose pinometostat treatment was able to reduce the viability of EOL-1 xenografts in rats without affecting HOXA9 expression.
source: This finding is congruent with and potentially explains how low-dose pinometostat treatment was able to reduce the viability of EOL-1 xenografts in rats without affecting HOXA9 expression (Kühn et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from published literature and connected to the current findings.

claim: There was no observable reduction in STAT5A phosphorylation in EOL-1 cells after 7 days 100 nM pinometostat.
source: There was no observable reduction in STAT5A phosphorylation after 7 days 100 nM pinometostat (Figure 4J), consistent with previous studies showing that WT FLT3 has little effect on STAT5A activation (Choudhary et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 4J.

claim: WT FLT3 has little effect on STAT5A activation.
source: There was no observable reduction in STAT5A phosphorylation after 7 days 100 nM pinometostat (Figure 4J), consistent with previous studies showing that WT FLT3 has little effect on STAT5A activation (Choudhary et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: WT FLT3 is typically upregulated by MLL-fusions and is able to activate other pathways involved in cell growth and proliferation such as PI3K/AKT.
source: WT FLT3 is typically upregulated by MLL-fusions and is able to activate other pathways involved in cell growth and proliferation such as PI3K/AKT (Armstrong et al., 2002; Cauchy et al., 2015; Choudhary et al., 2005)
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: One or more FLT3-activated growth signaling pathways may be essential for EOL-1 and MLL-PTD leukemia cell survival.
source: One or more of these FLT3-activated growth signaling pathways may be essential for EOL-1 and MLL-PTD leukemia cell survival just as the STAT5A signaling pathway appears to be for FLT3-ITD leukemia.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data.

claim: H299R and S711F mutations create a constitutively active murine Stat5a able to activate target genes independently of upstream signaling.
source: Previous work showed that H299R and S711F mutations create a constitutively active murine Stat5a able to activate target genes independently of upstream signaling (Onishi et al., 1998), which phenocopies the effects of exogenous FLT3-ITD expression including hyperproliferation and inhibition of myeloid maturation (Moore et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Constitutively active Stat5a phenocopies the effects of exogenous FLT3-ITD expression including hyperproliferation and inhibition of myeloid maturation.
source: Previous work showed that H299R and S711F mutations create a constitutively active murine Stat5a able to activate target genes independently of upstream signaling (Onishi et al., 1998), which phenocopies the effects of exogenous FLT3-ITD expression including hyperproliferation and inhibition of myeloid maturation (Moore et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Ectopic expression of STAT5A-CA was able to partially rescue proliferation when challenged with 30 nM FLT3 inhibitor tandutinib.
source: Ectopic expression of STAT5A-CA was able to partially rescue proliferation when challenged with 30 nM FLT3 inhibitor tandutinib, confirming the capacity of this mutant to complement impaired FLT3-ITD signaling (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: STAT5A-CA overexpression rescued pinometostat-induced proliferation reductions.
source: Remarkably, STAT5A-CA overexpression also rescued pinometostat-induced proliferation reductions (Figure 5B) in proportion to each clone's STAT5A-CA expression level (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 5B.
