claim: The degree of proliferation rescue from STAT5A-CA overexpression corresponded to each clone's STAT5A-CA expression level.
source: Remarkably, STAT5A-CA overexpression also rescued pinometostat-induced proliferation reductions (Figure 5B) in proportion to each clone's STAT5A-CA expression level (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing expression and proliferation data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: MEF2C overexpression displayed no effect on the viability of MV4;11 cells treated with 100 nM pinometostat.
source: As another control, we similarly overexpressed MEF2C, yet it displayed no effect on the viability of MV4;11 cells treated with 100 nM pinometostat (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Expression of STAT5A-CA restored expression of PIM1, PIM2, and ARID3B in both DOT1L inhibitor- and FLT3 inhibitor-treated MV4;11 cells.
source: To gain a molecular understanding of how ectopic STAT5A-CA expression could rescue proliferation of inhibitor-treated cells, we measured expression of the STAT5A targets PIM1, PIM2, and ARID3B by RT-qPCR. Expression of STAT5A-CA restored expression of PIM1, PIM2, and ARID3B in both DOT1L inhibitor- and FLT3 inhibitor-treated MV4;11 cells (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: ~30% of MV4;11 cells treated with 1 µM pinometostat for 6 days were undergoing apoptosis.
source: A previous study observed that ~30% of MV4;11 cells treated with 1 µM pinometostat for 6 days were undergoing apoptosis (Daigle et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: 25.5 ± 0.3% of MV4;11 cells were apoptotic when treating with 1 µM pinometostat for 7 days.
source: We analyzed apoptosis in MV4;11 cells treated with increasing concentrations of pinometostat for 7 days (Figure 5D and E). We observed 25.5 ± 0.3% apoptotic cells when treating with 1 µM pinometostat and a still sizeable proportion (15 ± 1%) of apoptotic cells when treating with just 100 nM pinometostat.
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry data shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: 15 ± 1% of MV4;11 cells were apoptotic when treating with 100 nM pinometostat for 7 days.
source: We analyzed apoptosis in MV4;11 cells treated with increasing concentrations of pinometostat for 7 days (Figure 5D and E). We observed 25.5 ± 0.3% apoptotic cells when treating with 1 µM pinometostat and a still sizeable proportion (15 ± 1%) of apoptotic cells when treating with just 100 nM pinometostat.
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry data shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: Treatment of STAT5A-CA clone 1 with 100 nM pinometostat for 7 days resulted in no significant induction of apoptosis compared to the DMSO control.
source: Yet upon treatment of STAT5A-CA clone 1 with 100 nM pinometostat for 7 days, we observed no significant induction of apoptosis as compared to the DMSO control (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry data shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: Recovering STAT5A function can rescue MV4;11 cells from apoptosis induced by 100 nM pinometostat.
source: Thus, we concluded that recovering STAT5A function can rescue MV4;11 cells from apoptosis induced by 100 nM pinometostat.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the apoptosis rescue data.

claim: One signaling pathway, FLT3-ITD to STAT5A, is able to account for the bulk of the phenotypic and molecular changes caused by low-dose DOT1L inhibition.
source: It is striking that despite marked gene expression changes caused by low-dose DOT1L inhibition, one signaling pathway, FLT3-ITD to STAT5A, is able to account for the bulk of the phenotypic and molecular changes we measured.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's data.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat downregulated the repressive PRC2 complex members EZH2 and EED.
source: One potential explanation for this effect is the downregulation of the repressive PRC2 complex members EZH2 and EED and consequent reductions in global levels of the transcriptionally repressive H3K27me3 mark (Figure 6A–B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figures 6A-B.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat caused consequent reductions in global levels of H3K27me3.
source: One potential explanation for this effect is the downregulation of the repressive PRC2 complex members EZH2 and EED and consequent reductions in global levels of the transcriptionally repressive H3K27me3 mark (Figure 6A–B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: PRC2 deposits the facultative heterochromatin H3K27me3 modification.
source: PRC2 deposits the facultative heterochromatin H3K27me3 modification and, although antagonistic to MLL1 and H3K4me3 deposition (Kim et al., 2013), is necessary for MLL-r leukemogenesis (Shi et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2011; Neff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: PRC2 is antagonistic to MLL1 and H3K4me3 deposition.
source: PRC2 deposits the facultative heterochromatin H3K27me3 modification and, although antagonistic to MLL1 and H3K4me3 deposition (Kim et al., 2013), is necessary for MLL-r leukemogenesis (Shi et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2011; Neff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: PRC2 is necessary for MLL-r leukemogenesis.
source: PRC2 deposits the facultative heterochromatin H3K27me3 modification and, although antagonistic to MLL1 and H3K4me3 deposition (Kim et al., 2013), is necessary for MLL-r leukemogenesis (Shi et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2011; Neff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: 100 nM pinometostat decreased H3K27me3 genome-wide as measured by quantitative ICeChIP.
source: Analysis by quantitative ICeChIP revealed that 100 nM pinometostat decreased H3K27me3 genome-wide (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Promoter H3K27me3 levels are reduced by 2–5% on average with pinometostat treatment.
source: Promoter H3K27me3 levels are reduced by 2–5% on average with more pronounced decreases observed among downregulated genes and MLL-AF4 targets than upregulated or all genes (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: H3K27me3 levels in untreated cells were much higher in pinometostat-upregulated genes.
source: However, H3K27me3 levels in untreated cells were much higher in pinometostat-upregulated genes, perhaps indicating that these genes are more reliant on PRC2 to buffer their expression.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data.

claim: Pinometostat-upregulated genes may be more reliant on PRC2 to buffer their expression.
source: However, H3K27me3 levels in untreated cells were much higher in pinometostat-upregulated genes, perhaps indicating that these genes are more reliant on PRC2 to buffer their expression.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data.

claim: EI1 treatment had comparatively little effect on the class of genes massively overexpressed during DOT1L inhibition.
source: EI1 treatment had comparatively little effect on the class of genes massively overexpressed during DOT1L inhibition (Figure 6E, compare to Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: EZH2 inhibition downregulated HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression.
source: Surprisingly, EZH2 inhibition downregulated HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression (which only occurs with higher doses of pinometostat Daigle et al., 2013), with no changes in FLT3 expression (Figure 6F) or STAT5 phosphorylation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: EZH2 inhibition caused no changes in FLT3 expression or STAT5 phosphorylation.
source: Surprisingly, EZH2 inhibition downregulated HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression (which only occurs with higher doses of pinometostat Daigle et al., 2013), with no changes in FLT3 expression (Figure 6F) or STAT5 phosphorylation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The greater reduction in global H3K27me3 from 10 µM EI1 than 100 nM pinometostat may account for the lack of effect on HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression by pinometostat.
source: The greater reduction in global H3K27me3 from 10 µM EI1 than 100 nM pinometostat may account for the lack of effect on HOXA9 and MEIS1 expression by pinometostat.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data.

claim: The PRC2 pathway is largely independent of the FLT3-ITD-STAT5A pathway.
source: Collectively, these data argue that the PRC2 pathway is largely independent of the FLT3-ITD-STAT5A pathway, culminating in distinct target gene expression consequences, that may converge for only a few targets, such as PIM1 and ARID3B.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the data.

claim: Inducible overexpression of EZH2 was only able to partially rescue proliferation in M4;11 cells treated with pinometostat.
source: Next, we queried the functional consequences of rescuing EZH2 expression in the context of low-dose DOT1L inhibition. Inducible overexpression of EZH2 was only able to partially rescue proliferation in M4;11 cells treated with pinometostat, suggesting that a small portion of the effects on MV4;11 viability is due to reduced PRC2 function (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 6G.

claim: A small portion of the effects on MV4;11 viability from pinometostat is due to reduced PRC2 function.
source: Next, we queried the functional consequences of rescuing EZH2 expression in the context of low-dose DOT1L inhibition. Inducible overexpression of EZH2 was only able to partially rescue proliferation in M4;11 cells treated with pinometostat, suggesting that a small portion of the effects on MV4;11 viability is due to reduced PRC2 function (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is an inference from the rescue experiment data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The FLT3-ITD-STAT5A pathway is the predominant source of pinometostat-induced effects on proliferation in MV4;11 cells.
source: The nearly complete rescue from intervening in the FLT3-ITD-STAT5A pathway compared to the modest rescue from PRC2, suggests that the former is the predominant source of pinometostat-induced effects on proliferation in this leukemia background.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing rescue experiments.

claim: MI-503 competitively antagonizes binding of MENIN to MLL1.
source: MI-503 competitively antagonizes binding of MENIN to MLL1, an interaction that is necessary for MLL-fusion complex localization to target genes and leukemogenesis (Borkin et al., 2015; Li et al., 2013a; Yokoyama et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The MENIN-MLL1 interaction is necessary for MLL-fusion complex localization to target genes and leukemogenesis.
source: MI-503 competitively antagonizes binding of MENIN to MLL1, an interaction that is necessary for MLL-fusion complex localization to target genes and leukemogenesis (Borkin et al., 2015; Li et al., 2013a; Yokoyama et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MM-401 inhibits the methyltransferase activity of MLL1 by disrupting its interaction with WDR5.
source: Another small molecule, MM-401 inhibits the methyltransferase activity of MLL1 by disrupting its interaction with WDR5, a complex member necessary for full enzymatic activity of MLL1 but not MLL2-4 or SET1 complexes (Cao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: WDR5 is a complex member necessary for full enzymatic activity of MLL1 but not MLL2-4 or SET1 complexes.
source: Another small molecule, MM-401 inhibits the methyltransferase activity of MLL1 by disrupting its interaction with WDR5, a complex member necessary for full enzymatic activity of MLL1 but not MLL2-4 or SET1 complexes (Cao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: MLL-r, FLT3-ITD+ cells showed greater reductions in proliferation from low concentrations of MI-503 or MM-401 than their WT FLT3 counterparts.
source: We treated MLL-r cell lines with low concentrations of MI-503 or MM-401 and observed greater reductions in the proliferation of MLL-r, FLT3-ITD+ cells than their WT FLT3 counterparts (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: Pinometostat treatment increased H3K4me3 at transcription start sites genome-wide.
source: Surprisingly, pinometostat treatment increased H3K4me3 at transcription start sites (TSS's) genome-wide, with the largest increases at genes downregulated by pinometostat (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The largest increases in H3K4me3 from pinometostat treatment were at genes downregulated by pinometostat.
source: Surprisingly, pinometostat treatment increased H3K4me3 at transcription start sites (TSS's) genome-wide, with the largest increases at genes downregulated by pinometostat (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Pinometostat-downregulated MLL-AF4 targets had the highest H3K4me3 levels of all gene categories examined.
source: Pinometostat-downregulated MLL-AF4 targets had the highest H3K4me3 levels of all gene categories examined (Figure 7C), not only at the TSS but spreading downstream into the gene body, suggesting that the MLL-fusion protein is driving this increase.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The MLL-fusion protein is driving the increase in H3K4me3 at pinometostat-downregulated MLL-AF4 targets.
source: Pinometostat-downregulated MLL-AF4 targets had the highest H3K4me3 levels of all gene categories examined (Figure 7C), not only at the TSS but spreading downstream into the gene body, suggesting that the MLL-fusion protein is driving this increase.
evidence: This is an inference from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Similar H3K4me3 upregulation is observed after only 4 days of pinometostat treatment.
source: Similar upregulation is observed after only 4 days of pinometostat treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D), and in two additional ICeChIP-seq experiments at 7 days of treatment we observed increases in promoter H3K4me3 by qPCR consistent with our ICeChIP-seq results at genes up and downregulated by pinometostat as well as MLL-AF4 targets (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Reductions in H3K79me2 from pinometostat treatment are poorly correlated with increases in H3K4me3.
source: Reductions in H3K79me2 from pinometostat treatment are poorly correlated with increases in H3K4me3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H), incompatible with a direct antagonism cross-talk mechanism.
evidence: This is a finding from ICeChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The poor correlation between H3K79me2 reductions and H3K4me3 increases is incompatible with a direct antagonism cross-talk mechanism.
source: Reductions in H3K79me2 from pinometostat treatment are poorly correlated with increases in H3K4me3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H), incompatible with a direct antagonism cross-talk mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference from the data analysis.

claim: Despite gains of the H3K4me3 mark during treatment, genes are downregulated, consistent with a decoupling of active transcription initiation from productive elongation.
source: Despite gains of the H3K4me3 mark during treatment, these genes are downregulated, consistent with a decoupling of active transcription initiation from productive elongation, the latter of which is more effectively correlated with H3K79me2 and H3K36me3 (Guenther et al., 2007).
evidence: This is an inference from the data and cited literature.

claim: Productive elongation is more effectively correlated with H3K79me2 and H3K36me3.
source: Despite gains of the H3K4me3 mark during treatment, these genes are downregulated, consistent with a decoupling of active transcription initiation from productive elongation, the latter of which is more effectively correlated with H3K79me2 and H3K36me3 (Guenther et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The increase in H3K4me3 is not due to iterative methylation by MLL1 associated with a stalled pol II.
source: However, when examining H3K4me3 fold changes stratified by gene expression level, we do not observe larger increases in H3K4me3 at more transcriptionally active genes, suggesting that the increase in H3K4me3 is not due to iterative methylation by MLL1 associated with a stalled pol II (Figure 7—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is an inference from data analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The putative antagonism between H3K79me2 and H3K4me3 modifications is not apparent in global H3K4me3 levels during DOT1L inhibition.
source: Intriguingly, the putative antagonism between modifications is not apparent in global H3K4me3 levels during DOT1L inhibition (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Reductions in H3K4me3 from MLL1 inhibitor treatment are not readily apparent by Western blot.
source: However, reductions in H3K4me3 from MLL1 inhibitor treatment are also not readily apparent by Western blot, similar to what has been observed in other studies (Cao et al., 2014; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and cited literature.

claim: Global increases in H3K79me2 are more pronounced when treating cells with the MLL1 inhibitors.
source: Conversely, global increases in H3K79me2 are more pronounced when treating cells with the MLL1 inhibitors (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Treatment with the MLL1 inhibitors reduced STAT5A phosphorylation.
source: Treatment with the MLL1 inhibitors also reduced STAT5A phosphorylation, suggesting that this orthologous means of disrupting MLL-fusion gene activation also reduces FLT3-ITD/STAT5A signaling (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MLL1 inhibitors reduce FLT3-ITD/STAT5A signaling.
source: Treatment with the MLL1 inhibitors also reduced STAT5A phosphorylation, suggesting that this orthologous means of disrupting MLL-fusion gene activation also reduces FLT3-ITD/STAT5A signaling (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference from Western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Overexpression of STAT5A-CA was able to partially rescue survival of MV4;11 cells treated with MI-503.
source: As with the DOT1L and FLT3 inhibitors, overexpression of STAT5A-CA was able to partially rescue survival of MV4;11 cells treated with MI-503 (Figure 7D), with the degree of rescue corresponding to the amount of STAT5A expression in each clone (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 7D.

claim: STAT5A-CA clone 1 completely rescued proliferation when treated with the MM-401 inhibitor.
source: When treated with the MM-401 inhibitor, STAT5A-CA clone 1 (with the highest exogenous STAT5A-CA expression), completely rescued proliferation (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 7E.

claim: STAT5A-CA clones 2 and 3 displayed reduced proliferation when treated with MM-401 compared to WT or GFP-expressing cells.
source: Unexpectedly, clones 2 and 3, that express STAT5A-CA at lower levels both displayed reduced proliferation when treated with MM-401 compared to WT or GFP-expressing cells (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 7E.

claim: An additive effect on proliferation was observed when MV4;11 cells were co-treated with the MLL1 and DOT1L inhibitors.
source: We observed an additive effect on proliferation when MV4;11 cells were co-treated with the MLL1 and DOT1L inhibitors (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F), suggesting that either the inhibitors target different sets of genes through different mechanisms, or have an additive effect on the same genes.
evidence: This is a finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: MI-503 reduced expression of FLT3, MEF2C, ARID3B and PIM1.
source: Akin to low dose DOT1L inhibitor treatment, MI-503 reduced expression of FLT3, MEF2C, ARID3B and PIM1.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data.

claim: The reduction in FLT3 expression from MI-503 was only 30 ± 10% but doubled to 60 ± 10% when both MI-503 and pinometostat were used.
source: The reduction in FLT3 expression was only 30 ± 10% but doubled to 60 ± 10% when both inhibitors were used, recapitulating the 60% reduction observed with pinometostat alone.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data.

claim: MI-503 had no significant effect on PBX3 expression.
source: MI-503 had no significant effect on PBX3 expression but both inhibitors reduced PBX3 expression to 50 ± 10%, the same as the DOT1L inhibitor alone.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data.

claim: MI-503 treatment starkly reduced expression of HOXA9 and MEIS1.
source: However, unlike low-dose pinometostat, MI-503 treatment starkly reduced expression of HOXA9 and MEIS1 and combination treatment further reduced MEIS1 expression from 40% to 30%.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data.

claim: Combination treatment of MI-503 and pinometostat further reduced MEIS1 expression from 40% to 30%.
source: However, unlike low-dose pinometostat, MI-503 treatment starkly reduced expression of HOXA9 and MEIS1 and combination treatment further reduced MEIS1 expression from 40% to 30%.
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data.

claim: Low dose MLL1 and DOT1L inhibitors downregulate different, yet partially overlapping sets of genes that are necessary for MLL-rearranged leukemia.
source: Taken together, low dose MLL1 and DOT1L inhibitors downregulate different, yet partially overlapping sets of genes (with FLT3, MEF2C, and PIM1 in common), that are necessary for MLL-rearranged leukemia, consistent with the synergism arising from largely distinct pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the gene expression data.

claim: STAT5A-CA-mediated rescue of proliferation in MV4;11 cells treated with MI-503 coincided with increased expression of STAT5A target genes PIM1, PIM2, and ARID3B.
source: We examined expression of these targets in our 3 STAT5A-CA clones after treating cells with MI-503 for 7 days and observed increased expression of the STAT5A target genes PIM1, PIM2, and ARID3B (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a finding from RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Downregulation of FLT3-ITD and reductions in STAT5A phosphorylation and gene activation are more sensitive to perturbations of MLL-fusion-mediated gene activation than HOXA9 and MEIS1 in MLL-r, FLT3ITD leukemias.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that downregulation of FLT3-ITD, and crucially, reductions in STAT5A phosphorylation and gene activation are more sensitive to perturbations of MLL-fusion-mediated gene activation and are the main source of inhibitor effects on leukemia cell survival when expression of the canonical MLL-r proliferation mediators HOXA9 and MEIS1 are not substantially affected (model, Figure 7—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's data.
